A native spline loft, three independent silhouette comparisons, and the limits of the public drawing.

10 SEP 2026PREPARED FOR: BRAD ROTHENBERGREVISION 2

00 / PURPOSEMatch the fuselage before adding the aircraft.

The requested scope is the clean fuselage skin. Sensors, antennas, gun barrels, wings, engines, and empennage are excluded. The notebook keeps the source model's 9.144 m length and uses its guide-driven loft method.

Measured result

The plan and side views exceed 99.5%. The front view does not.

The final silhouette overlaps are 99.834% in plan, 99.865% from the side, and 92.698% from the front. These are comparisons to the frozen public-drawing traces.

Deliver
Use the editable native loft and the measured overlays below.
Unmet
The requested threshold must pass in all three views. This reconstruction does not satisfy that condition.
Resolve
Use a consistent dimensional three-view or measured fuselage sections to resolve the front-view discrepancy.

03 / SOURCE CONSISTENCYThe front view does not share the same body envelope.

Source quantityView AView BDifference (derived)
Maximum body heightSide: 141.074 pxFront: 131.223 px9.850 px; 7.51% of front height
Maximum body widthPlan: 100.737 pxFront: 103.000 px2.263 px; 2.20% of front width
Precision limit

Under the fixed orthographic registration, the traced envelopes disagree before model fitting. The height difference is 55.9 mm at the 9.144 m CAD scale (derived). Source orientation and hidden-skin boundaries are not dimensioned. The front overlay also contains profile and symmetry differences. This score is not a proof of the best possible fit.

A front silhouette does not identify the section at each fuselage station. This loft uses that silhouette as a transverse shape prior. Its interior section distribution is inferred. No measured section table or survey tolerance was found in the sources used here.

A high score against a traced raster cannot establish 99.5% agreement with the physical aircraft. Stroke thickness, hidden skin, configuration differences, and the inconsistent envelopes remain unresolved.

04 / NATIVE CONSTRUCTIONUse the source model's loft technique.

Four longitudinal cubic spline guides control width, crown, keel, and lateral datum. Each guide has 100 control points. A 28-control-point transverse spline forms the rounded section. Explicit longitudinal and section bounds close the solid.

The source notebook supplies the guide-driven modeling technique. A native spline distance field replaces the initial conic profile to fit the public front-view shape. Length, width, and height remain editable. Native geometry blocks create the surface.

VerificationMeasured resultEvidence
Field signs and guide values73 / 73 checks passInterior, exterior, crown, keel, guide readback, and cap bounds.

Saved notebookOne visible fuselage; seven collapsed sectionsAPI recipe export, presentation audit, and native renders.
Input model preservationOriginal input SHA-256 unchangedThe revised model is a separate R2 file.
Registration and scoring details

The source skin extends from image x = 716 to x = 2327. These endpoints set the 1611 px body length. One isotropic scale maps that length to 9.144 m. Source-only translations set the lateral center and midrange height. No view receives an independent aspect stretch.

Native pixels enter the mask when alpha exceeds 127. The reference polygon is evaluated at the same world-space camera pixel centers. No erosion, dilation, uncertainty exclusion, or background pixels contribute to the IoU score.

The small end section has a half-size of 0.1 source pixel, or 0.568 mm at the default CAD scale (derived). This keeps the native distance field defined at the nose.
